newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen up on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen up on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares on Wednesday fell after a two-day rise and analysts said the stronger post-price- fixing buying signalled growth on Thursday, with the market then flat or up slightly amid a lack of negative signals.
"All signals outside the market seem either to be neutral or positive," said Artur Nagorka, a trader at Wood & Company.
Analysts said a signal likely to be taken neutrally or positively by the market could come on Monday, when the August inflation figure, expected to be around last year's 0.4 percent, is announced.
They said this number followed by a good September figure could lead to a cut in official interest rates.
Analysts said firms' August earnings figures due next week, expected to match July's results in being slightly better than the first half's mediocre numbers, should spur some stocks.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.5 percent to 13,818.1 points and turnover fell 19.2 percent to 80.4 million zlotys ($28.9 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 36 to 23 with 18 stocks flat.

Some analysts said greater interest in mass privatisation NFI units, which rose 5.9 percent in record 57.9-million-zloty ($20.8 million) trade, were drawing capital from shares. The units have jumped 43.7 percent since August 29.
In continuous trade they jumped seven percent to 133.3 zlotys ($47.9). In live trade food trader Rolimpex, the only stock to see action, rose 1.7 percent to 123 zlotys ($44.2).
Analysts said biggest loser insurer Warta fell 5.8 percent in profit-taking after rising 20 percent this week on a 12.8-million-zloty ($4.6 million) return of interest in overpaid tax.
Steel trader Stalexport, which fell 2.8 percent in session- high 10.3-million-zloty ($3.7 million) trade, awaits a court decision on Thursday for 75 million zlotys in interest on overpaid tax.
